findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a trash bag in the upright cooler to be storing flatbread. Trash bags are not considered smooth, easily cleanable, or food safe. Ensure all food items are stored in permitted packaging moving forward.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a stack of clean cutting boards to be stored between cardboard boxes of gloves and cardboard boxes containing soda syrup. The PIC was informed that these cardboard surfaces are not considered clean or food safe. Ensure equipment and utensils are stored on food-grade, clean surfaces to prevent cross contamination. The cutting boards were relocated during today’s visit.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior of the upright freezer in the kitchen to have an excessive accumulation of frost. Ensure the freezer is defrosted regularly to prevent frost contamination with food in the freezer. This freezer will be inspected again during the next routine inspection to ensure defrost has been completed.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a black debris. The PIC was informed that the ice machine needs to be deep cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on June 15, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no employee health/reporting agreements available or signed by staff. Education was conducted regarding this document and its importance to food safety. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure this document is signed by all staff and on file in the facility for the inspector to view.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no written procedure for vomit/diarrhea incidents in the facility. Education was conducted with the PIC and a policy was provided. The facility has bleach available for conducting the procedure. Ensure this policy is maintained on file for employees to refer to in the event of a vomit/diarrheal event in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no non-latex gloves available at the bar for garnish handling. The PIC stated that their current practice for peeling oranges for garnish does not include wearing gloves. Edible flowers and cherries were also observed to be bare handed during today’s visit. Inspector conducted food handling education. The PIC was informed that all ready-to-eat foods must be handled with clean, gloved hands at all times. Ensure gloves are used in the future to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no hand washing sign present at the bar/kitchen hand sink or two bathroom hand sinks. The PIC was informed and hand washing signs were provided. Ensure these signs are posted by all three handwashing sinks and are clearly visible for all staff to view.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the PIC use the bar/kitchen hand sink to empty/refill the sanitizer bucket. The bucket was temporarily stored in the sink basin. Education was conducted regarding hand sinks. Ensure hand sinks are for hand washing only. Hand sinks cannot be obstructed under any conditions, especially since the facility only has one sink for the bar and kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the bar/kitchen sanitizer bucket measure 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer was not strong enough, and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the bucket is monitored for proper chemical concentration. The sanitizer will weaken over time and must be replaced frequently.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a black debris. The PIC was informed that the ice machine needs to be deep cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a container of pico de gallo in the prep cooler top measure 55F with the infrared probe. The pico de gallo was stored in a plastic container within a metal container in the cooler. This “doubling” prevents adequate air movement and refrigeration of the container. Since the pico de gallo had no date mark and the PIC did not know when the item was prepared, the container was discarded. Ensure proper cold holding is monitored with a stem thermometer. Storage in the prep cooler needs to promote proper cooling. A spot check will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored properly in the cooler and maintaining a temperature of 41F or less at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following food items to be missing a date mark:

1. Pico de gallo
2. Shrimp
3. Sausage
4. Pork pieces

The PIC was informed that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and ready-to-eat (RTE) foods must be date marked within 24 hours of opening/prepping. These items must be discarded within 7 days of marking. A handout was provided with extra details regarding proper date marking methods. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure proper date marking practices are taking place in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometers stored in the prep cooler or upright cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and plans to acquire thermometers for the cooler. Ensure all coolers have ambient thermometers prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple dishes to be stored on a top shelf with their food contact surfaces exposed to splash and dust. The PIC was informed that the items need to be inverted to prevent contamination. Ensure these items are properly stored prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available at the facility. Quaternary ammonia is in use as sanitizer in both the sanitizer buckets and triple sink. The PIC was informed and stated she could not find the test strips. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to confirm test strip availability. Inspector recommends having extra packs of test strips available to prevent future violations.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the seams of the wall paneling to be bubbling and separating. A white tape was used in areas to seal the seams, but this tape is already separating from the wall. Ensure the wall is repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the PIC describe inaccurate food handling procedures in the facility. The PIC stated that oranges and other garnishes are not handled with gloved hands. The inspector also observed the PIC training new staff on beverage preparation. The PIC was observed bare handing cherries, edible flowers, and citrus garnishes during this training event. The person in charge is responsible for knowing, understanding, and accurately communicating proper food handling procedures to staff members in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 regarding the PIC's knowledge of proper food handling practices in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.
